subject: Computer Networking
title: Digital Signatures
description: A micro-lesson that makes Digital Signatures usable.

hook.text: How do you prove an email really came from the sender? A digital signature makes forgery mathematically impossible.

buildup.text: The sender hashes the message and encrypts the hash with their private key. That encrypted hash is the signature.

discovery.text: Anyone with the sender's public key can decrypt the signature and compare it to their own hash of the message.

twist.text: If even one character changed in transit, the hashes won't match. Tampering is instantly detected.

climax.text: Software updates, legal documents, and TLS certificates all use digital signatures to prove authenticity.

punchline.text: A digital signature proves who sent it and that nothing changed.

quiz.question: What does a digital signature prove?
options: The sender's identity and that the message wasn't altered
That the message was encrypted during transmission
That the recipient has read the message

details.summary: Digital signatures use asymmetric cryptography to prove a message was sent by a specific person and has not been altered. The signer hashes the message and encrypts the hash with their private key. Anyone with the public key can decrypt the hash and verify it matches the message.
details.whyItMatters: Digital signatures provide non-repudiation and integrity for documents, software updates, code signing, and financial transactions. They are the digital equivalent of a handwritten signature with even stronger guarantees.
takeaways: Signatures prove both the sender's identity and message integrity
The signer's private key creates the signature; the public key verifies it
Non-repudiation means the signer cannot deny having signed

faq.question: How are digital signatures different from encryption?
faq.answer: Encryption hides message content using the recipient's public key. Digital signatures prove the sender's identity using the sender's private key. A signed message is not necessarily encrypted — it is readable by anyone but verifiably from the signer.

faq.question: Where are digital signatures used in practice?
faq.answer: Software updates are signed to prevent tampering. HTTPS certificates are digitally signed by certificate authorities. Email can be signed with S/MIME or PGP. Code signing verifies that applications come from trusted developers. Legal documents are signed digitally in many jurisdictions.
